# Flux Download Manager 1.0.0

Flux is now available as a self-contained Windows x64 desktop application. Recipients do not need Node.js or development tools.

## Choose a download

- **Flux-Download-Manager-1.0.0-x64-setup.exe** — recommended installer with desktop and Start menu shortcuts.
- **Flux-Download-Manager-1.0.0-x64-portable.exe** — portable application; run it directly without installing.
- **SHA256SUMS.txt** — checksums for verifying both executable files.

## Features

- Up to 16 parallel HTTP(S) segments per download
- Pause, safe resume, retry, cancel, restart, and crash recovery
- Persistent queue, priorities, scheduling, and concurrent-download limits
- Per-download and global bandwidth limits
- Live speed, progress, transferred size, and ETA
- Optional SHA-256 integrity verification
- Collision-safe filenames and atomic final-file placement
- Automatic takeover of Chromium-browser downloads strictly larger than 6 GB
- Authenticated browser handoff with cookies and referrer information
- Search, filters, categories, light/dark themes, notifications, and activity history
- Native file/folder actions and a Windows system tray mode
- Local-only service bound to `127.0.0.1`, with no analytics or cloud account

## Browser capture setup

Open Flux, go to Settings, and choose **Set up browser capture**. On the browser extension page, enable Developer mode, choose **Load unpacked**, and select the folder Flux opens. Downloads of 6 GB or less stay in the browser; only larger HTTP(S) downloads are handed to Flux.

## Windows warning

This first community release is not code-signed. Windows SmartScreen may display an “unrecognized app” warning. Verify the executable against `SHA256SUMS.txt`, inspect the public source if desired, then use **More info → Run anyway** only if you trust the download.
